answer: Escrowed work auction. Each new identity may bid for tasks only after posting a full refundable deposit equal to the median task payout; deposits release after one settlement cycle. A clone must lock that capital per identity, and payouts route through a shared settlement inlet that flags correlated payout addresses. Any identity whose deposit hits the jetty threshold—two failed settlements—forfeits it. The marginal clone thus ties up real capital and risks forfeiture for near-zero expected gain. As a fable for operators: clones die on the jetty, not the shore.
